bibliography.independence_note: MeMOTR and MOTIP are from the same group (Gao & Wang, MCG-NJU), share the Deformable-DETR/MOTR code lineage and the same benchmarks (DanceTrack, SportsMOT); they are NOT independent confirmations of each other. MeMOT is from an independent group but belongs to the same end-to-end transformer MOT family (MOTR-style clip training). Preprint and conference versions of each paper are the same work, counted once.

full_text_checked: MOTIP: arXiv HTML v2 read through a fetch/summarisation tool (characters 0-100000 of 105238; Tables 1-6, 9, Sections 3.4, 4.2, 5, Appendix B.3 checked; Table 4 checkmark columns not recoverable, so the row-to-component mapping is uncertain); code files read directly: models/runtime_tracker.py (constructor, _get_activate_detections, _get_id_pred_labels, _hungarian_assignment, _assign_newborn_id_labels), models/motip/id_criterion.py, configs/r50_deformable_detr_motip_dancetrack.yaml, README.md. MeMOTR: arXiv HTML v3 read through a fetch/summarisation tool (Sections 3.3-3.5, 4.7, Tables 1-7, 10) and README.md; Table 6 rows were ambiguous in the extracted text; supplementary not opened; code not opened. MeMOT: full arXiv PDF (11 pages) extracted locally to text and read for Sections 3.2-4.6 including Tables 2-8 verbatim; Table 1 rows partially read; no supplementary/appendix beyond the PDF; no official code exists to check. CVF open-access versions were not opened separately (assumed equal to the latest arXiv versions).
inputs_state_output: All three take full RGB frames (shorter side 800) through a ResNet-50 backbone plus a Deformable-DETR (MeMOTR: DAB-Deformable-DETR) transformer encoder, COCO-pretrained; per-object features are 256-d decoder query embeddings, not region-pooled. MOTIP: state = for every live trajectory the last T frames (T=29 DanceTrack, 59 SportsMOT, 19 BFT; code MISS_TOLERANCE 30) of DETR output embeddings, each concatenated with a learnable ID-dictionary embedding (K=50, K+1-th token = 'newborn'), giving 2C-dim tracklet tokens; a 6-layer transformer ID decoder lets current detections (queries) attend to ALL trajectories' tokens jointly (in-context) with relative temporal position encoding; output = K+1-way ID distribution per detection. MeMOTR: state = per-track long-term memory updated by EMA M <- (1-lambda)M + lambda*O with lambda=0.01, only when confidence > 0.5, plus the previous-frame output; a memory-attention layer and adaptive aggregation produce the next-frame track query; output = box and score per track query (identity is inherited by the query). MeMOT: state = FIFO spatio-temporal memory X in R^{N x T x d}, Nmax 300/600 tracks, Tmax 24 (22 used for MOT16/17, 20 for MOT20); short-term cross-attention over last Ts=3 states queried by the latest state, long-term cross-attention over Tl=24 states queried by a dynamically updated learnable token (DMAT), fusion -> track embedding; a memory decoder takes [proposal queries, track queries] against the image features and outputs box, objectness and uniqueness per entry. Comparison with ours: our per-target state is FlyVis recurrent activity over a bounded grey crop (exemplar + search frames) for ONE track at a time; the readout sees 68 region-pooled activity features per real detection region, an observed-target descriptor from a ridge model fit on 4 exemplar frames, 8 geometry inputs and 6 scalar assignment-context features. We have no per-track multi-frame token memory, no descriptors of neighbouring tracks (only their scalar costs), and descriptors exist only for regions inside the eye and only when the prior query had supported regions (14252 of 37296 queries). Their memories assume an embedding for every detection of every track in every frame, which our eye cannot supply.
action_and_refusal: MOTIP: the action is assigning an ID label to each detection above det_thresh (0.3); refusal/new is represented by a learnable 'newborn' class (index K) in the same softmax; a detection keeps an existing ID only if its probability exceeds id_thresh (0.2), otherwise it becomes newborn if score > newborn_thresh (0.6) or is dropped. Code shows assignment protocols 'hungarian', 'object-max', 'id-max'; the DanceTrack config uses object-max (per-detection argmax), consistent with the paper's statement that Hungarian is not used by default and gives no considerable benefit. In the Hungarian variant the newborn column is replicated so several detections can be newborn. Lost tracks are kept for 30 frames. MeMOTR: action = track query emits box/score; tracks with score <= 0.5 become inactive and are removed after T_miss frames (30 DanceTrack, 15 MOT17, 10 BDD100K); newborns from detect queries with score > 0.5. MeMOT: every proposal and track entry gets confidence s = objectness x uniqueness; entries above a threshold epsilon are kept; proposals that duplicate a tracked object are suppressed via uniqueness 0; no post-processing. None of them has an explicit 'keep the tracker's own default decision' option, because they ARE the tracker; abstention is a learned class (MOTIP) or a learned score factor (MeMOT) trained with the same loss as the decisions. Ours: full-box transfer from a selected real region into the track state before native ByteTrack matching, with a FIXED logit 0 for no action that is not trained; the closest analogue is MOTIP's learnable newborn/none token trained jointly with cross-entropy.
labels_and_loss: MOTIP: labels are ground-truth identities in sampled clips; each GT identity in a clip is mapped to a random ID-dictionary slot, objects not yet seen in the history get the newborn label; loss = focal classification 2.0 + L1 5.0 + GIoU 2.0 + ID cross-entropy 1.0 (code id_criterion.py: CE or optional sigmoid focal loss, normalised by the number of ID predictions, first frame excluded). Imbalance is not reweighted explicitly; robustness comes from trajectory augmentation: random token dropping (occlusion prob 0.5) and random ID swapping (prob 0.5) inside the history (config AUG_TRAJECTORY_OCCLUSION_PROB / SWITCH_PROB 0.5). Labels are dense: every detection in every frame is supervised. MeMOTR: MOTR-style clip training (clip length 2 -> 5 on DanceTrack) with set-prediction losses; details of the loss/assignment are not spelled out in the paper text read. MeMOT: GT assignment per Fig. 4: track entries get objectness by presence; proposals get boxes by bipartite matching and uniqueness = 1 only if the matched object has not been tracked before (tracked -> 1/1, new -> 1/1, background -> 0/1, suppressed duplicate -> 1/0); loss = 2*(focal objectness + focal uniqueness) + 5*L1 + 2*GIoU plus an auxiliary DETR detection loss; clip-centric training, clip length 2 increasing every 20 epochs, frame interval 1-10. None uses decision-consequence labels (good-minus-harm relative to a baseline tracker) and none treats rare corrective events specially; all labels are identity or detection correctness. Ours: MSE regression of each action score to good-minus-harm in {-1,0,+1}, most rows neutral, very few outcome-changing positives.
data_camera_resolution_rate: MOTIP: DanceTrack, SportsMOT, BFT (main, trained separately with detection pre-training), MOT17 in appendix (Table 7); input shorter side up to 800 with multi-scale augmentation (config: 480-800, max 1440); clips of 30 frames (config SAMPLE_LENGTHS 30), ablations with T=19; DanceTrack: largely uniform-appearance dancers, mostly fixed camera; SportsMOT: broadcast sports with camera motion; BFT: birds. Video counts not verified here (DanceTrack about 100 videos 40/25/35, SportsMOT about 240 videos 45/45/150) [uncertain]. MeMOTR: DanceTrack (main), MOT17 (+CrowdHuman), BDD100K (val, multi-class), SportsMOT; shorter side 800, max 1536. MeMOT: trained on MOT17 train + CrowdHuman val for MOT16/17, MOT20 alone; ablations trained on MOT17 train and validated on MOT15 train with overlapping videos removed (very few independent videos); shorter side 800; 8x A100. Frame rates: DanceTrack 20 fps, MOT17 mostly 30 fps, BDD100K MOT annotations at 5 fps [uncertain]. Initial conditions: tracks are born from detections with learned/thresholded scores; no external tracker. Ours: BDD100K MOT, grey bounded crop, YOLO26s run at 960, reused train26 and fit20 video subsets, external ByteTrack baseline.

distinguishing_ablations: All ablations are single runs, no seeds or confidence intervals reported. MOTIP (DanceTrack val): Table 5 association formulation with FROZEN detector features (two-stage: DETR trained, frozen, association trained separately): id-prediction HOTA 55.4 / AssA 41.1 / IDF1 55.7 vs re-id 29.4 / 11.5 / 22.1 vs contrastive 41.0 / 22.6 / 36.4; one-stage: id-pred 59.5 vs re-id 41.0 (re-id with trick 50.6) vs best contrastive 54.5 -> the formulation (classification over in-context IDs with CE) matters more than the features, and joint training adds about +4.1 HOTA. Table 6 trajectory augmentation (occlusion, swap): (0,0) 59.5; (0.5,0) 60.7; (1.0,0) 58.6; (0.5,0.2) 61.6; (0.5,0.5) 62.2; (0.5,0.8) 59.8. Table 9 ID-decoder depth: 1 layer 54.3, 3 57.6, 6 59.5, 9 60.5, 12 60.3. Table 4 components (self-attention among detections, Hungarian, augmentation): range 57.7 to 62.2 HOTA; Hungarian gives no considerable benefit; exact row mapping uncertain. No numeric ablation of trajectory length T, relative position encoding or learnable vs one-hot ID tokens. Limitation: ID dictionary capacity K, token utilisation < 40%; MOT17 weaker due to data diversity. MeMOTR (DanceTrack val): Table 7 EMA update rate lambda 0.005 -> HOTA 62.6 / AssA 53.1; 0.01 -> 63.9 / 55.0; 0.02 -> 63.2 / 53.5; 0.04 -> 63.5 / 54.0 (non-monotonic, about 1.3 HOTA range); Table 5 adaptive aggregation 62.3 -> 63.9 HOTA with both components (text claims +2.6, table shows +1.6: internal inconsistency); Table 6 memory + memory-attention 63.9 vs memory alone 62.5 HOTA (row mapping partly ambiguous); attention without memory reported to reduce AssA by 1.4. No temporal-length ablation. Limitations: newborns suppressed by tracked targets in self-attention, overfitting on small pedestrian sets. MeMOT (trimmed 2-layer models, MOT17 train -> MOT15 train val): Table 3 long-term length Tl 3/5/10/20/24 -> HOTA 59.09/59.31/59.53/59.85/59.75, IDF1 71.27/71.70/71.66/72.83/73.15, IDsw 136/136/117/96/93 (max 24 due to GPU memory); Table 2 short-term Ts 2/3/4/5 -> HOTA 58.99/59.75/59.51/59.48; Table 5 heuristic pooling of memory collapses (average T=3 IDF1 25.04 HOTA 21.89; max T=24 HOTA 6.54) vs attention 73.15/59.75; Table 6 single cross-attention without short/long split T=24 HOTA 58.73, IDsw 99; Table 4 learnable tokens for both branches IDF1 41.09 HOTA 43.28 (collapse), latest-observation query for short-term is essential; Table 7 no DMAT update HOTA 49.24 vs 59.75; Table 8 single confidence head HOTA 52.86 vs dual objectness x uniqueness 59.75 (separating 'not an object' from 'not new' matters). Mandatory components for the claimed effect: learned attention-based reading of memory (not pooling), dense identity supervision, joint context of all tracks/detections; memory length itself gives modest gains (about +0.7 HOTA, +1.9 IDF1 from Tl 3 to 24 in MeMOT).

explanations_addressed.lost_discriminative_spatial_info_in_read: Caution / design analogy. MeMOT Table 5 shows that crude averaging or max-pooling of per-object embeddings over time destroys identity information (HOTA 59.75 -> 21.89 or lower), and MOTIP shows a 6-layer attention decoder clearly beats 1 layer (59.5 vs 54.3). This is temporal pooling of 256-d DETR embeddings, not spatial pooling of FlyVis activity, so it does not directly test our 68 region-pooled features; it only warns that fixed pooling plus a shallow head can be the bottleneck.
explanations_addressed.target_vs_neighbour_identification: Direct design analogy. MOTIP decodes every current detection against the histories of all live tracks simultaneously (in-context), with self-attention among detections and ID-swap augmentation that explicitly trains confusions between tracks; MeMOT's uniqueness head learns whether a proposal duplicates an already-tracked object. Our readout sees neighbours only as scalar costs (best competing track cost) and has no FlyVis descriptor of the neighbour, so it cannot learn 'this region belongs to the other track'.
explanations_addressed.training_objective_mismatched_to_final_a: Direct evidence within their setting. MOTIP Table 5: same frozen features, only the formulation changes: ID classification with CE 55.4 HOTA vs re-id 29.4 vs contrastive 41.0; the trained distribution is exactly the inference decision (argmax over K+1 incl. newborn). MeMOT Table 8: separating objectness and uniqueness heads 59.75 vs single ambiguous score 52.86 HOTA. Both support training the decision distribution (including the abstain/none class) end-to-end instead of regressing per-action scores and comparing against an untrained fixed logit 0, which conflates 'baseline already right' with 'cannot tell'.
explanations_addressed.rare_useful_events_with_high_harm_cost: Not addressed. All three train on dense identity/detection labels where nearly every row is informative; no cost-sensitive loss, no notion of improvement over a baseline tracker, thresholds (MOTIP id 0.2, newborn 0.6) hand-set. Dense identity correctness would mostly reward cases where ByteTrack is already right (our 1000-3500 selected rows with only 13-33 outcome changes), so this mechanism alone does not solve the rarity problem.
explanations_addressed.insufficient_history: Direct but modest evidence. MeMOT Table 3: Tl 3 -> 24 gives HOTA +0.66, IDF1 +1.88, IDsw 136 -> 93; MeMOTR Table 7 slow EMA (lambda 0.01) best, about 1.3 HOTA range; MOTIP trajectory occlusion augmentation (dropping history tokens with p 0.5) +1.2 HOTA, combined with ID swap +2.7. History helps, but only when an embedding exists for each past frame. Our coverage gap (history available for 14252 of 37296 queries; restricted oracle +2.07 pp) is a data-availability problem: memory architectures do not create descriptors for frames where FlyVis never looked; token-dropout augmentation only makes a head robust to missing history.
explanations_addressed.limits_of_the_action: Not addressed / caution. Their action is the identity (and box) of every detection, produced by the tracker itself; there is no 'override an external tracker' action and no separate gain estimate. MeMOTR on BDD100K keeps inactive tracks only 10 frames. Nothing here informs the 334 cases with the correct detection outside our eye.

evidence_strength: Peer-reviewed: MeMOT CVPR 2022 Oral, MeMOTR ICCV 2023, MOTIP CVPR 2025. Code verified to exist and inspected for MOTIP (inference thresholds, newborn handling, ID loss); MeMOTR code exists (README checked, code not opened); MeMOT has no official code. MeMOTR and MOTIP share authors and code lineage (not independent). Ablations are single runs without seeds or intervals, on validation sets (MeMOT ablations on very few MOT15 videos). Overall: moderate for the claim that ID-classification with a learnable none class and attention-read memory beats re-id/contrastive/pooled association under strong jointly trained RGB features; weak for transfer to our setting (734-parameter FlyVis, 68 pooled grey features, external tracker, rare corrective events).
difference_from_tried: Differs in four concrete ways: (1) loss: cross-entropy over the identity of each real region among {this track, neighbouring tracks, none} with a LEARNED none/newborn class, versus our per-action MSE good-minus-harm regression plus an untrained fixed logit 0 and a softmax threshold; (2) context: descriptors of competing tracks' histories are present as tokens, versus our 6 scalar assignment-context features; (3) history: multi-frame token memory (up to 30 frames) read by attention, versus a ridge target model on 4 exemplar frames; (4) training-time augmentation: random history token dropping and ID swapping. It is NOT different in kind from the already failed learned 3-peak association (KeepTrack-inspired) and the ridge target model insofar as both are identity matching of candidates to one target; the genuinely untried parts are the learned none class trained with the same CE as the choice, neighbour-track tokens, and history dropout/swap augmentation. Category replacement and context features did not include any of these.
candidate_node_change: Node: readout + loss (and an optional per-track state buffer of readout outputs). Change: replace the per-action MSE head by an in-context identity head (MOTIP-style, small: 1-2 attention layers, d about 64): tokens = FlyVis readout descriptors of this track from exemplar frames and earlier supported queries, plus descriptors of the competing track(s) when available, each tagged with a slot embedding; queries = the 68-feature regional descriptors (+8 geometry) of current real regions; output = softmax over {this track, competitor slot(s), learnable none}. Loss: CE on ground-truth identity of each region (dense), with history-token dropout p 0.5 and slot-swap augmentation; MeMOT-style second head separating 'region is a valid object' from 'region belongs to this track' if needed. Action rule: transfer the full box of the region only when argmax = this track, it differs from the ByteTrack assignment, and p(this track) - p(none) exceeds a threshold chosen on fit20. Why it addresses a FlyVis problem: the current readout does not separate target from neighbour and its abstain logit is untrained (objective mismatch), which matches the measured facts (selects 1000-3500 rows, 13-33 outcome changes, probability never above about 0.6). Equal controls with identical head, data, threshold protocol: old D readout, stock FlyVis C, eye-input R1 (same regions pooled from the grey crop without FlyVis), no-fly geometry-only head; the FlyVis claim requires the FlyVis version to beat both R1 and geometry-only. Cheap CPU check on saved features: on reused train26/fit20 rows with saved 68 features, compute (a) top-1 identity accuracy and target-vs-neighbour AUROC on the 1001 wrong baseline assignments and specifically on the 553 cases with the correct detection inside the eye, (b) offline replay of the action rule: number of good vs harmful transfers on fit20 at the chosen threshold, all for FlyVis vs R1 vs geometry-only. Proceed to replay HOTA / GPU only if the FlyVis head recovers clearly more of the 553 inside-eye errors than R1 and geometry-only with harmful transfers no larger than fixed ones, and the restricted oracle (history-covered queries, +2.07 pp) is the stated ceiling. GPU stage (new FlyVis maps) only if the check passes and the remaining limit is history coverage or missing neighbour descriptors, e.g. running FlyVis eyes for competitor tracks or on queries without supported prior regions.
strongest_objection: The reported gains come from strong, jointly trained 256-d RGB embeddings (ResNet-50 + 6-layer Deformable-DETR encoder, video-trained on 8 GPUs) with an embedding for every detection of every track in every frame; even MOTIP's frozen-feature variant uses those DETR features. Our 68 region-pooled features from a 734-parameter grey-input model exist only inside one track's eye and only for 38% of queries, and our previous identity-style heads (fixed/learned 3-peak association, ridge target model) already failed. Dense identity CE would be dominated by the easy majority where ByteTrack is already right and does not target the rare outcome-changing events; the expected ceiling is the history-restricted oracle +2.07 pp, already near the +2 pp criterion, so even a perfect identity head over covered queries may not pass. Furthermore, MOTIP itself trails heuristic trackers on MOT17, so end-to-end identity prediction is not shown to beat a tuned ByteTrack-type association.
cost_and_hardware: Bounded adaptation (small attention/CE head on saved FlyVis features, geometry and R1 controls, 24-seed style repetition) fits on CPU in roughly hours with existing saved features. New FlyVis maps for neighbour tracks or uncovered queries would need GPU passes on one 12 GB card (crop-level, feasible in hours). Replicating MOTIP/MeMOTR/MeMOT end to end is out of scope: 8 GPUs (MeMOT 8x A100, 200 epochs; MeMOTR recommends >= 32 GB GPUs or about 10 GB per GPU with gradient checkpointing across 8 GPUs) and an RGB DETR backbone, which would also not be a FlyVis modernisation.
